conclusion: Pillar 0 is not 'merge 104 branches'. Branch-level merges would be destructive: the nearest branches still differ by roughly 50 files, and the large ones delete 179-289 files that main has. Any transfer of work must be per-file, chosen by content, and judged by tests -- which is exactly the discipline already applied to the repair engine. A bulk merge was never on the table and is now measured out.
corrections_recorded: Pass 1 reported 'arena/0eb6c191-brain differs in 0 files'. The branch object does not exist locally (it was deleted after PR #7069 merged), so two failing commands produced empty output that was read as agreement. The squash claim now rests only on the commit message, which is what it actually is.

Pass 2 reported 'readable: 0' for all 104 branches because `git branch -r` indents each line by two spaces and the leading whitespace was kept when building ref names. Every lookup was malformed. Fixed by stripping before use; the numbers here come from the corrected pass.
headline: main holds a single commit. None of the 104 live arena branches has a tree identical to it, and 84 of them differ in 200+ files. The branches share a different root (a6ef30b89f, 'Establish private Project Brain staging substrate'), so git reports them ~23,000 commits ahead of main while they are really a parallel lineage.
method: git plumbing only; every command's exit code recorded so a failure cannot be read as a zero.
what_this_does_not_establish: Not evidence that the branches lack useful work, nor that their contents conflict. Only that a bulk merge is destructive and that 'unmerged' is not 'pending'.
